target.name: PvZ 1.0.0.1051 EN (local-engine extracted executable)
target.avz_reference: inc/avz_pvz_struct.h (State @0x28, Hp @0xC8, IsDisappeared @0xEC, AtWave @0x6C) and src/avz_asm.cpp (KillZombie=0x5302F0, RemoveZombie=0x530510)

method: Read-only static disassembly of the locked executable (llvm-objdump 23 from the pinned LLVM-MinGW 20260908 toolchain), cross-referenced with the pinned AvZ framework constants. No game process, no live memory inspection, no hook installed.
protocol_notes: All VA values are absolute addresses in the locked image loaded at 0x400000; RVA = VA - 0x400000.
The AvZ framework independently hard-codes KillZombie=0x5302F0 and RemoveZombie=0x530510; this disassembly is consistent with those entry points.
A byte-pattern scan of the full .text for `movb $1, 0xec(reg)` found exactly one site: 0x530602 inside 0x530510.
No production hook may be implemented from this file alone; the issue's junior gate requires maintainer review of these candidates first.

candidates.semantics: Marks a zombie as removed and detaches it; the slot is freed later by the 0x41BAD0 sweep.
observed: Detaches movement/grid state via 0x530850 and attached references at +0x110/+0x118/+0x144/+0x150.
Sets the AvZ IsDisappeared() byte at +0xEC to 1.
A byte-pattern scan of the full .text found exactly one `movb $1, 0xec(reg)` site: 0x530602 here.
Calls 0x52FE50 (drop/loot housekeeping) and type-specific handlers for types 0x0D, 0x14, 0x19.
Returns without freeing the pool slot; the slot is freed later by 0x41BAD0 once +0xEC is set.
candidates.candidate_classification: Primary candidate for the `zombie-removal-unclassified` fact: one shared function marks any removed zombie, including death removals; a consumer must pair it with a prior death-stage observation to classify a death removal.
coverage_limits: Does not distinguish death from non-death removal by itself (KillZombie 0x5302F0 calls it first).
Callers include preview/UI-looking paths (0x4019A8/0x4019DD) that may not be board zombies.
Not yet verified whether every board removal reaches this function (bungee/flag/lawnmower paths need per-caller review).
open_questions: Confirm the +0xEC writer is unique across the whole image (only one byte-pattern site; data-driven writes still possible).
Confirm which callers are board removals vs preview/menu objects.
Decide whether classification needs the death-stage event or a caller/RVA field on the removal record.
